rot.carlsbad.ideia.teoria.e1: Attack: this is the Carlsbad structure, from the Queen's Gambit Declined, Exchange Variation. White traded the c-pawn and kept d4 and e3; Black kept c6 and d5.
rot.carlsbad.ideia.teoria.e2: On the queenside, White has two pawns against three. Advancing this minority to trade pawns and leave a weak black pawn is the minority attack. The a- and b-pawns have already moved up.
rot.carlsbad.ideia.teoria.l1: The b4-pawn advances to b5 and attacks the c6-pawn.
rot.carlsbad.ideia.teoria.l2: Black captures with the a-pawn. If Black waited, the b5-pawn would capture on c6 anyway.
rot.carlsbad.ideia.teoria.l3: The a4-pawn recaptures and attacks the c6-pawn again.
rot.carlsbad.ideia.teoria.l4: The black rook takes the a-file, opened by the trade, and attacks the knight on c3, which the queen and the other knight defend.
rot.carlsbad.ideia.teoria.l5: The b5-pawn captures the one on c6: this is the trade the minority attack was after.
rot.carlsbad.ideia.teoria.l6: Black recaptures with the b-pawn. If Black recaptured with the bishop, the d5-pawn would be isolated.
rot.carlsbad.ideia.teoria.l7: Now the c6-pawn is backward, on a half-open file, and the c5-square has become weak. The minority attack did not win material: it left a target for the rest of the game.
rot.carlsbad.ideia.minoria.e1: Attack: White again, now in a game played on Lichess. The black pawn on d5 is isolated: there is no black pawn on the c- and e-files.
rot.carlsbad.ideia.minoria.e2: The queen on b3 attacks the d5-pawn, and the queen on c6 defends it. Your pawns on a4 and b4 still face the black pawns on a6 and b7.
rot.carlsbad.ideia.minoria.p: Find the minority-attack move that removes the defender of the d5-pawn.
rot.carlsbad.ideia.minoria.certo: The pawn advances to b5 and attacks the queen on c6, the piece that defends the d5-pawn.
rot.carlsbad.ideia.minoria.revela: The pawn advances to b5 and attacks the queen on c6: she will have to move, and the d5-pawn loses its defender.
rot.carlsbad.ideia.minoria.err.b3d5.1: The queen captures the d5-pawn, but the queen on c6 defends it.
rot.carlsbad.ideia.minoria.err.b3d5.2: The black queen recaptures, and White is left without the queen.
rot.carlsbad.ideia.minoria.err.b3d5.3: Back to the position: before capturing the d5-pawn, remove its defender.
rot.carlsbad.ideia.minoria.err.c5b7.1: The knight captures the b7-pawn, but the queen on c6 attacks it, and no white piece defends it.
rot.carlsbad.ideia.minoria.err.c5b7.2: The queen captures the knight, and White is a piece down.
rot.carlsbad.ideia.minoria.err.c5b7.3: Back to the position: use a queenside pawn.
rot.carlsbad.ideia.minoria.fora: That move does not attack the defender of the d5-pawn. Use the b4-pawn or the queen on b3.
rot.carlsbad.ideia.minoria.volta: Try again: remove the defender of the d5-pawn.
rot.carlsbad.ideia.minoria.l0: On b5, the pawn attacks the queen on c6.
rot.carlsbad.ideia.minoria.l1: Black captures the pawn. If the queen went to d6, the knight would capture the b7-pawn.
rot.carlsbad.ideia.minoria.l2: The a4-pawn recaptures and attacks the queen again.
rot.carlsbad.ideia.minoria.l3: The queen goes to b6, where she attacks the knight on c5, but she no longer defends the d5-pawn.
rot.carlsbad.ideia.minoria.l4: The white queen captures the d5-pawn, which has been left undefended.
rot.carlsbad.ideia.minoria.l5: The advance of the b-pawn did not attack the isolated pawn: it attacked its defender. In positions like this, the minority attack opens the way for the pieces to reach the target.
rot.carlsbad.ideia.alvo.e1: Attack: White again, in another Lichess game. After the minority attack, the black pawn on c6 has become backward: the one on d5 has already gone ahead, and there is no black pawn on the b-file.
rot.carlsbad.ideia.alvo.e2: The c-file is half-open for White, and the queen on c2 attacks the c6-pawn along it. No black piece defends it.
rot.carlsbad.ideia.alvo.p: Find the move that captures the backward pawn.
rot.carlsbad.ideia.alvo.certo: The queen captures the c6-pawn and attacks the rook on a8 and the bishop on c8 at the same time.
rot.carlsbad.ideia.alvo.revela: The queen captures the c6-pawn along the half-open file and makes a double attack: the rook on a8 and the bishop on c8.
rot.carlsbad.ideia.alvo.err.b1b7.1: The rook enters b7 along the b-file, but the bishop on c8 attacks it, and no white piece defends it.
rot.carlsbad.ideia.alvo.err.b1b7.2: The bishop captures the rook, and White is a rook down.
rot.carlsbad.ideia.alvo.err.b1b7.3: Back to the position: capture the c6-pawn along the half-open file.
rot.carlsbad.ideia.alvo.err.c2c5.1: The queen goes to c5 and attacks the d5-pawn, but the queen on g5 defends it.
rot.carlsbad.ideia.alvo.err.c2c5.2: The bishop goes to d7 and now defends the c6-pawn: the target is no longer loose.
rot.carlsbad.ideia.alvo.err.c2c5.3: Back to the position: the c6-pawn is undefended. Capture it.
rot.carlsbad.ideia.alvo.fora: That move does not capture the c6-pawn. Use the piece that already attacks it along the c-file.
rot.carlsbad.ideia.alvo.volta: Try again: capture the backward pawn.
rot.carlsbad.ideia.alvo.l0: On c6, the queen attacks the rook on a8 and the bishop on c8.
rot.carlsbad.ideia.alvo.l1: The bishop goes to b7: it attacks the queen and defends the rook on a8.
rot.carlsbad.ideia.alvo.l2: The rook on b1 captures the bishop along the b-file, opened by the minority attack.
rot.carlsbad.ideia.alvo.l3: The backward pawn was left alone, and the white pieces reached it. In positions like this, after the minority attack, the b- and c-files are the road for the rooks and the queen.
rot.carlsbad.demos.regra.1: Attack demonstration: White again, in another Lichess game. Black has the pawns on c6 and d5, as in the Carlsbad, and the c6-pawn is on the c-file, in front of your rook.
rot.carlsbad.demos.regra.2: The b7-pawn defends the one on c6, but it is pinned: if it left the b-file, the king would be in check from the queen on b6.
rot.carlsbad.demos.regra.l.3: The knight on e5 captures the c6-pawn with check.
rot.carlsbad.demos.regra.l.4: The b7-pawn cannot recapture. If the king stepped out of check, the queen on b6 would capture the one on c7. So the queen captures the knight.
rot.carlsbad.demos.regra.l.5: The rook on c1 captures the queen along the c-file.
rot.carlsbad.demos.regra.l.6: White gave the knight and won the queen. In positions like this, the c6-pawn is what closes the c-file: when it falls, the rook comes in along it.
rot.carlsbad.demos.regra2.1: Attack demonstration: now let us think from Black's side, in another Lichess game, in the same opening. In the Carlsbad, the d5-pawn watches the e4-square.
rot.carlsbad.demos.regra2.2: The white knight on e4 defends the bishop on g5. The d5-pawn attacks that knight and, at the same time, closes the fifth rank between the queen on a5 and the bishop.
rot.carlsbad.demos.regra2.l.3: The d5-pawn captures the knight, and the fifth rank opens: the queen on a5 now attacks the bishop on g5.
rot.carlsbad.demos.regra2.l.4: The bishop on d3 recaptures the pawn. If the bishop on g5 ran away, Black would have captured the knight for free.
rot.carlsbad.demos.regra2.l.5: The queen captures the bishop on g5, which has been left undefended.
rot.carlsbad.demos.regra2.l.6: Black captured the knight and the bishop and gave only a pawn. In the Carlsbad, the d5-pawn is Black's strength: before putting a piece on e4, count who attacks it and what it defends.
rot.carlsbad.demos.excecao.1: Attack demonstration: White again, in another Lichess game. The structure is Carlsbad, but here the white pieces are already close to the black king.
rot.carlsbad.demos.excecao.2: The queen on d6 attacks the rook on f8, and the rook on f3 attacks the one on f7. On the f-file, the black rooks defend each other.
rot.carlsbad.demos.excecao.l.3: The queen captures the rook on f8 with check.
rot.carlsbad.demos.excecao.l.4: The rook on f7 recaptures the queen: it is the only move against the check.
rot.carlsbad.demos.excecao.l.5: The f-file is now free, and the rook on f3 captures on f8 with check: it is mate.
rot.carlsbad.demos.excecao.l.6: Here the minority attack did not even start: the pieces were already aiming at the king, and mate decided. The Carlsbad does not force anyone to play on the queenside: the position decides.
rot.carlsbad.pratica.valeAqui.enunciado: The structure is Carlsbad, and your pieces are close to the white king. Is it worth thinking about the queenside here? Play as Black and find the best move.
rot.carlsbad.pratica.valeAqui.fim: The queen gave check on h2, and the king went to f1. The queen came in on h1: it is mate. Here the attack on the king decided before any queenside plan.
rot.carlsbad.pratica.cravada.enunciado: The black pawn on c6 defends the bishop on b5, and the black queen stands behind it, on the c-file. Play as White and find the best move.
rot.carlsbad.pratica.cravada.fim: The queen captured the bishop on b5. The c6-pawn cannot recapture: the rook on c1 pins it against the queen on c7. With no way to save the material, the black queen tried a check on h2, and the king captured it.
rot.carlsbad.pratica.valeAqui.err2.h3g2: 27...Bxg2+? The bishop captures the bishop on g2 with check, but 28.Qxg2 trades queens, and the attack on the king is over. Your queen has a move that ends the game.
rot.carlsbad.pratica.cravada.err.a5a6: 26.a6? The pawn advances, but it gives Black time: the black queen leaves the c-file, and the c6-pawn defends the bishop on b5 with no risk of a pin.
rot.carlsbad.pratica.cravada.err.c1b1: 26.Rb1? The rook attacks the bishop on b5, but leaves the c-file. It is the rook that would pin the c6-pawn against the queen on c7, if your queen left the file.
rot.carlsbad.pratica.cravada.err.c5b6: 26.Qb6? The queen offers the trade and leaves the bishop on b5 alone. If she captured it, the c-file would open, and the c6-pawn would be pinned against the queen on c7.
rot.carlsbad.pratica.cravada.err.e3e4: 26.e4? The pawn attacks the one on d5, but it gives Black time: the black queen leaves the c-file, and the c6-pawn defends the bishop on b5 with no risk of a pin.
rot.carlsbad.pratica.cravada.err.g1f2: 26.Kf2? The king leaves g1, but it gives Black time: the black queen leaves the c-file, captures the h2-pawn, and the c6-pawn defends the bishop on b5 with no risk of a pin.
rot.carlsbad.pratica.cravada.err2.g1f2: 27.Kf2? The king steps out of check, but the black queen has already left c7: the c6-pawn is no longer pinned, and 27...cxb5 captures your queen. The queen on h2 is within reach of your king.
rot.carlsbad.pratica.valeAqui.err.h3g2: 26...Bxg2? The bishop captures the bishop on g2, but 27.Qxg4 captures the knight, and the attack on the king is over. Your queen has a check that comes first.
rot.carlsbad.pratica.valeAqui.err.g3g2: 26...Qxg2+? The queen captures the bishop on g2 with check, but 27.Qxg2 captures her, and after 27...Bxg2 28.Kxg2 the queens are off the board: the attack on the king is over. Your queen has another check.
rot.carlsbad.pratica.valeAqui.err.g4e3: 26...Nxe3? The knight captures the e3-pawn, but 27.Bxe3 captures it, and Black loses the attacking knight. Your queen has a check that leads to mate.
rot.carlsbad.pratica.troca.enunciado: The black bishop on c6 stands on the open c-file, within reach of your b5-pawn. Play as White and find the best move.
rot.carlsbad.pratica.troca.fim: The queen captured the bishop on c6, and the black queen captured her. The b5-pawn recaptured and reached c6, as in the minority attack. Without the black queen, your bishop on d6 is safe: White has won a piece.
rot.carlsbad.pratica.troca.err.b5c6: 26.bxc6? The pawn captures the bishop, but 26...Qxd6 captures your bishop on d6, which was loose, and the trade comes out even. Before capturing with the pawn, look at what the black queen attacks.
rot.carlsbad.pratica.troca.err.c2c5: 26.Qc5? The queen defends the bishop on d6, but the bishop on c6 is still defended by the black queen, and the advantage is gone.
rot.carlsbad.pratica.troca.err.d6c5: 26.Bc5? The bishop escapes the black queen's attack, but 26...Bxb5 captures your b5-pawn, and Black is two pawns up.
rot.carlsbad.pratica.troca.err.d6a3: 26.Ba3? The bishop escapes the black queen's attack, but 26...Bxb5 captures your b5-pawn, and Black is two pawns up.
rot.carlsbad.pratica.troca.err.d6b4: 26.Bb4? The bishop escapes the black queen's attack, but 26...Bxb5 captures your b5-pawn, and Black is two pawns up.
rot.carlsbad.pratica.troca.err.d6f4: 26.Bf4? The bishop escapes the black queen's attack, but 26...Bxb5 captures your b5-pawn, and Black is two pawns up.
